In the plant's maintenance bay, Joseph finished the last line of the start-up checklist and signed the sheet. Oil level, belt tension, safety guard: all ticked. It was the same card Joseph had used on the old press for three years. The new press had been installed on Monday.

Sarita, the shift supervisor, read the sheet at ten and pressed the green button. Around noon a thin line of coolant sprayed from a joint near the pump. Sarita hit the emergency stop, and the crew stepped back while a fitter closed the valve. Production stopped for the afternoon.

Later Joseph stood holding the card. Every box was ticked, and none of them mentioned that pump. "I did what the sheet said," Joseph said quietly.

"So did I," said Sarita. "The sheet didn't know this machine."

qa.q: What did Sarita do when the coolant sprayed?
What was Joseph probably feeling while holding the card afterwards?
qa.a: Joseph probably felt uneasy and let down, having trusted the card when every box was ticked and the fault was still missed.

qa.q: What could Joseph do next time a new machine arrives?
qa.a: Joseph could read the new machine's manual, add lines for what is different, and look at the machine with fresh eyes before signing instead of ticking automatically.

qa.q: How might Sarita see the incident?
qa.a: Sarita may feel partly responsible too, having relied on the signed sheet, and be worried about the lost afternoon.

grounding: Shows a technician ticking a familiar checklist that has no line for a new machine's fault, giving false confidence.

Dear Akash,
You asked me to write down what went wrong at the Sonepat plant, so you can share it with the new technicians. Here it is, honestly.
On the 14th, I did the monthly check on the new packing machine. I used the same checklist we use for the old ones: belts, oil level, sensors, emergency stop, guard doors. Every line was fine. I ticked all twenty and signed.
What I didn't think about was that this new model has a heating unit for sealing. The old ones don't. Nothing on the list mentions heat. The seal bar was running too hot, and I never looked.
Two days later it scorched a batch and the line stopped for six hours.
The list made me feel I had checked everything, when I had only checked the old machine's problems.
Please tell the team: a new machine needs new questions.
Siddharth

qa.q: How many lines did Siddharth tick on the checklist?
qa.a: Siddharth ticked all twenty and signed.

qa.q: How does Siddharth seem to feel writing this letter?
qa.a: Siddharth seems regretful and honest, admitting the list gave a false sense of having checked everything.

qa.q: What would you change first in how the new machine was checked?
qa.a: Before using the old list, ask what is different about the new machine and add lines for those parts, such as the heating unit.

qa.q: How might the new technicians be affected by this letter?
qa.a: They may feel warned and more careful, knowing not to trust an old checklist on a new machine.

grounding: It shows a technician running the usual checklist on a new machine and signing off, while a fault no line covers goes unnoticed.

Kalyani, you asked why I'm so fussy about checklists now. Let Abhinav tell you about the X-ray room at the clinic, last winter.
We'd just got a new digital machine. I was the technician on duty. I had the old daily checklist, twenty lines, and I'd done it maybe three hundred times. Power, cooling fan, cables, lead aprons, door warning light. Tick, tick, tick. Signed at 8.05.
But the new machine had a software step the old one didn't: a calibration check that shows a small warning on the screen. It isn't on the list. I didn't read the screen. The list said everything was fine, so I felt fine.
By eleven, a doctor noticed the images were coming out blurry. We had to call back six patients.
I followed every line perfectly. That was the problem. The list only knew the old machine.

qa.q: What time did Abhinav sign the checklist?
How did Abhinav feel after ticking all the lines?
qa.a: Abhinav felt fine and confident, because the list said everything was fine, though that confidence turned out to be false.

qa.q: What else could Abhinav have done with the new machine, and why?
qa.a: Abhinav could have read the new machine's screen and manual and added its checks to the list, since the old list only knew the old machine.

qa.q: How were the six patients affected?
qa.a: They had to be called back, which may have worried them and cost them time and another visit.
